usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 니
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
께 is the polite form of 에게/한테 for elders
examples: My grandmother lives in the countryside.
할머니 as the topic with 는
할머니 as the subject with 가
할머니 as the object with 를
nuance: 할머니 means grandmother and is used for both your father's and your mother's mother in everyday speech. To clearly mark the mother's side, you can say 외할머니. It is also a warm, polite way to address any elderly woman you are close to, similar to calling someone grandma.
mistakes: Writing 할머니이에요 instead of the correct 할머니예요 after the vowel.
Calling a middle-aged woman 할머니; it can feel rude, so use 아주머니 unless she is truly elderly.

usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 지
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
께 is the polite particle used for elders
examples: 할아버지 as the topic with 는
할아버지 as the subject with 가
I take a walk with my grandfather.
nuance: 할아버지 means grandfather and covers both sides of the family in casual speech, while 외할아버지 specifies the mother's father. Like 할머니, it can also be a respectful way to address an elderly man you know. Note the spelling: it is 할아버지, written together, not 할 아버지.
mistakes: Writing 할아버지이에요 instead of the correct 할아버지예요.
Splitting it as 할 아버지; the word for grandfather is one word, 할아버지.

usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 니
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
댁 is the polite word for an elder's home
examples: My maternal grandmother lives in Busan.
외할머니 as the topic with 는
My maternal grandmother gave me pocket money.
외할머니 as the subject; 주셨어요 is the honorific past
I went to my maternal grandmother's house during the break.
nuance: 외할머니 means your mother's mother, with 외 marking the maternal side of the family. In casual speech many people just say 할머니 for both grandmothers, but 외할머니 makes the side clear. The matching word for your mother's father is 외할아버지.
mistakes: Writing 외할머니이에요 instead of the correct 외할머니예요.
Using 외할머니 for your father's mother; the father's side is just 할머니 (or 친할머니).

usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 지
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
께 is the polite particle for elders
examples: 외할아버지 as the topic with 는
My maternal grandfather told me old stories.
외할아버지 as the subject; 해 주셨어요 is honorific
I take after my maternal grandfather.
외할아버지 as the object with 를
nuance: 외할아버지 means your mother's father, where 외 signals the maternal side. As with grandmothers, casual speech often uses plain 할아버지 for both, but 외할아버지 removes any confusion. The female counterpart on the same side is 외할머니.
mistakes: Writing 외할아버지이에요 instead of the correct 외할아버지예요.
Using 외할아버지 for your father's father; that side is just 할아버지 (or 친할아버지).

usage: noun + 이에요 after the consonant ㄴ
with subject marker 이 after a consonant
examples: My uncle works at a company.
삼촌 as the topic with 은
My uncle gave me a birthday present.
삼촌 as the subject with 이
I play soccer with my uncle.
nuance: 삼촌 usually refers to your father's brother and is the everyday word young people use for an uncle. It is also a friendly way for children to address a close adult man. Your mother's brother is more precisely called 외삼촌, while your father's sister is 고모.
mistakes: Saying 삼촌예요 — after the consonant ㄴ it must be 삼촌이에요.
Using 삼촌 for your mother's brother; that is 외삼촌 when you need to be specific.

usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 모
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
a friendly way to call a female server
examples: 이모 as the topic with 는
이모 as the subject with 가
Ma'am, please give us some water here.
이모 used to call a female restaurant worker
nuance: 이모 means your mother's sister and is a warm, close word, often used even for your mother's close female friends. In restaurants, customers also call a friendly female server 이모, which sounds familiar and kind. Your father's sister is 고모, a different word.
mistakes: Writing 이모이에요 instead of the correct 이모예요.
Mixing up 이모 (mother's sister) with 고모 (father's sister); they are different relatives.

usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 모
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
examples: 고모 as the topic with 는
My aunt came to our house.
고모 as the subject with 가
고모 as the object with 를
nuance: 고모 means your father's sister, in contrast with 이모, who is your mother's sister. Korean keeps the two sides of the family separate with different words, so the side matters when you choose. Her husband is called 고모부.
mistakes: Writing 고모이에요 instead of the correct 고모예요.
Calling your mother's sister 고모; on the mother's side you must say 이모.

usage: the child of your aunt or uncle
noun + 이에요 after the consonant ㄴ
with subject marker 이 after a consonant
examples: My cousin is older than me.
사촌 as the topic with 은
My cousin came over to my house.
사촌 as the subject with 이
I get along well with my cousin.
nuance: 사촌 means a cousin, the child of your aunt or uncle on either side. To show whether the cousin is older or younger, Koreans often add a sibling word, as in 사촌 동생 (younger cousin) or 사촌 형/오빠/누나/언니. The number 사 (four) in 사촌 reflects the traditional way of counting family distance.
mistakes: Saying 사촌예요 — after the consonant ㄴ it must be 사촌이에요.
Calling a cousin just 형 or 누나 without 사촌; add 사촌 to make the relationship clear.

usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 카
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
examples: My niece/nephew is five years old now.
조카 as the topic with 는
조카 as the subject with 가
I bought a toy for my nephew/niece.
nuance: 조카 means your sibling's child and covers both nephew and niece, so the same word works for a boy or a girl. If you need to be specific, you can say 남자 조카 or 여자 조카, but 조카 alone is most common. From the child's point of view, you are their 삼촌, 이모, 고모, or 외삼촌.
mistakes: Writing 조카이에요 instead of the correct 조카예요.
Thinking 조카 is only a nephew; it means niece too, regardless of gender.

usage: family members beyond your immediate household
noun + 이에요 after the consonant ㄱ
with subject marker 이 after a consonant
examples: 친척 as the subject with 이
I went to a relative's house during the break.
친척 집 meaning a relative's home
nuance: 친척 means a relative or your relatives in general, including aunts, uncles, cousins, and more distant family. It is broader than 가족, which usually means your close, immediate family. Relatives most often gather during big holidays like 설날 and 추석, called 명절.
mistakes: Saying 친척예요 — after the consonant ㄱ it must be 친척이에요.
Using 친척 for your parents and siblings; close immediate family is usually 가족, not 친척.

usage: noun + 이에요 after the consonant ㄹ
with subject marker 이 after a consonant
examples: 아들 as the subject with 이
아들 as the subject with 이
아들 as the topic with 은
nuance: 아들 means son, your male child, and pairs with 딸 (daughter). Parents often say 우리 아들 (our son) as an affectionate way to refer to him. To count children you use the counter 명, as in 아들 한 명 (one son).
mistakes: Saying 아들예요 — after the consonant ㄹ it must be 아들이에요.
Confusing 아들 (son) with 아들들; for one son use 아들, and add 들 only for several sons.

usage: noun + 이에요 after the consonant ㄹ
with subject marker 이 after a consonant
examples: 딸 as the subject with 이
딸 as the subject with 이
딸 as the topic with 은
nuance: 딸 means daughter, your female child, and is the partner word to 아들 (son). Parents commonly say 우리 딸 (our daughter) with affection. The double consonant at the start, ㄸ, is a tense sound, so 딸 is pronounced more firmly than 달 (moon).
mistakes: Saying 딸예요 — after the consonant ㄹ it must be 딸이에요.
Pronouncing 딸 like 달 (moon); the tense ㄸ makes 딸 a stronger, different sound.

usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 자
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
examples: 손자 as the subject with 가
The grandson sits next to grandfather.
손자 as the subject with 가
Grandfather loves his grandson a lot.
손자 as the object with 를
nuance: 손자 means grandson, the son of your son or daughter, and is the word grandparents use. The matching word for a granddaughter is 손녀, and together 손자 손녀 means grandchildren. For grandchildren in general you can also say 손주.
mistakes: Writing 손자이에요 instead of the correct 손자예요.
Using 손자 for a granddaughter; a granddaughter is 손녀, not 손자.

usage: noun + 예요 after the vowel 녀
with subject marker 가 after a vowel
손녀 + 딸; a warm way to say it
examples: 손녀 as the subject with 가
The granddaughter writes a letter to grandmother.
손녀 as the subject; 한테 meaning to
손녀 as the object with 를
nuance: 손녀 means granddaughter, the daughter of your son or daughter, and pairs with 손자 (grandson). Grandparents sometimes say 손녀딸 affectionately. When talking about all grandchildren together, 손자 손녀 or 손주 is common.
mistakes: Writing 손녀이에요 instead of the correct 손녀예요.
Using 손녀 for a grandson; a grandson is 손자, not 손녀.
